metadata.title: ImageNet Classification with Deep Convolutional Neural Networks

summary.tldr: Ignited the modern deep learning revolution by training a large 8-layer CNN on GPUs to win the ImageNet ILSVRC-2012 competition by a massive 10.8 percentage point margin.
keyTakeaways: Introduced ReLU non-linearities to accelerate SGD training speed by 6x over Sigmoid/Tanh.
Used Dropout regularization to prevent severe overfitting in high-capacity fully connected layers.
Pioneered CUDA GPU parallelization across two NVIDIA GTX 580 GPUs.

motivation.problemStatement: Computer vision was stuck in a local minimum relying on manually engineered feature descriptors (SIFT, HOG). Deep neural networks were considered untrainable and computationally prohibitive on large-scale datasets.
previousLimitations: Tanh and Sigmoid activations caused severe vanishing gradient problems in multi-layer CNNs.
CPU computing hardware was too slow to train high-capacity networks on millions of images.
High-capacity networks overfitted rapidly on large parameter spaces.
motivation.coreInsight: Deep CNNs can be trained on massive high-resolution datasets if non-saturating ReLU activations are used to prevent gradient vanishing, combined with custom CUDA GPU kernels for parallel matrix multiplication.
contributions: Designed and trained AlexNet (5 convolutional layers, 3 fully connected layers).
Introduced ReLU (Rectified Linear Unit) activation to deep vision models.
Implemented Dropout regularization (p=0.5) in fully connected layers.

innovations.title: Non-Saturating ReLU Activation
innovations.summary: Replaces saturating Tanh/Sigmoid activations with f(x) = max(0, x), speeding up SGD convergence.
innovations.detailedDescription: Deep CNNs with saturating non-linearities take much longer to train than non-saturating ones. ReLU preserves constant unit gradient for positive inputs, preventing backpropagation signal decay.

math.explanation: Rectified Linear Unit formula outputting zero for negative inputs and linear identity for positive inputs.
math.significance: Accelerated SGD convergence time on CIFAR-10 by a factor of 6x compared to Tanh units.

innovations.title: Dropout Regularization
innovations.summary: Randomly zeros out neuron outputs with probability p=0.5 during training passes.
innovations.detailedDescription: Forces neurons to learn robust co-adapted features rather than relying on specific neighboring activation combinations, effectively ensembling an exponential number of sub-networks.

math.explanation: Bernoulli mask r_j applied to hidden layer activations during forward passes.
math.significance: Eliminated severe overfitting in FC6 and FC7 dense layers (containing 50M parameters).

ablationStudies.title: Impact of ReLU vs Tanh Activations
ablationStudies.description: Measured epoch count required to reach 25% training error rate on CIFAR-10.
ablationStudies.performanceDelta: ReLU reached 25% error in 5 epochs; Tanh required 30 epochs (6x slower convergence).

evidence.reproducibilityNotes: Trained for ~90 epochs across 5-6 days using two NVIDIA GTX 580 3GB GPUs.

criticalNotes.title: GPU Parallelization Landmark
criticalNotes.content: Proved that CUDA GPU hardware is the essential substrate for scaling deep learning models.

criticalNotes.title: Coarse Initial Convolutions
criticalNotes.content: 11x11 kernel size with stride 4 in Conv1 loses fine-grained low-level visual textures.

lineage.title: Gradient-Based Learning Applied to Document Recognition
lineage.description: Original ConvNet paradigm scaled up by AlexNet using GPUs.

lineage.title: Very Deep Convolutional Networks for Large-Scale Image Recognition
lineage.description: Replaced AlexNet's coarse 11x11 kernels with small uniform 3x3 stacks.

researchGaps: How to avoid large 11x11 filter parameters in early layers?
How to scale depth past 8 layers without parameter explosion?

reference.originalAbstract: We trained a large, deep convolutional neural network to classify the 1.2 million high-resolution images in the ImageNet LSVRC-2010 contest into the 1000 different classes. On the test data, we achieved top-1 and top-5 error rates of 37.5% and 17.0% which is considerably better than the previous state-of-the-art.

trainingDetails.optimizer: SGD with momentum 0.9 and weight decay 0.0005
